about: Plan 13e-3: pairs with a known domain motion, beside the random-100 two-state pairs, for the core-fit cut (diff.CORE_CUT). A is the reference (closed or liganded where the paper compares that way), B the other state. Domains are residue ranges of A's chain as the papers define them. Synthetic hinges: 1UBQ with residues 41-76 turned about residue 40's CA (the 13e-1 test, at four angles), the truth known exactly.

published.source: Sharff et al. 1992, Biochemistry 31:10657: maltose-free MBP (1OMP) opens by a ~35 degree rigid-body hinge bend of the two domains, with an ~8 degree twist, relative to the maltose complex (1ANF, Spurlino et al. 1991). Domains as Evenas et al. 2001 (J Mol Biol) give them: N 1-109, 264-309; C 114-258, 316-370.

Jameson et al. 1998, Acta Cryst D54:1319 (1CB6, apolactoferrin at 2.0 A; Norris et al. 1991 for 1LFH): the N-lobe opens by a 54 degree rotation of domain N2 relative to N1, against diferric lactoferrin (1LFG, Haridas et al. 1995); the C-lobe stays closed. Domains: N1 1-90, 251-333; N2 91-250; the C-lobe after the 334-344 helix.

Muller et al. 1996, Structure 4:147 (4AKE open, apo) and Muller and Schulz 1992 (1AKE, Ap5A): LID and NMP close over the substrates; no rotation angle was found stated in the abstracts read for this task. Domains: CORE 1-29, 68-117, 161-214; NMP 30-67; LID 118-160.
